summary: Elevated 5xx error-rate from API -> serving-runtime during short traffic spike (KV-cache thrash)
description:
Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-09 13:12 UTC we observed an increase in 5xx responses for a subset of requests from CartoStream routed through the us-east API gateway. Impact: ~12% elevated 5xx rate for their traffic over a 22-minute window; some requests returned 502/503 while others experienced long connection resets. Environment: Production (us-east) on Dedicated pool for CartoStream.

Observed behavior: API gateway logged upstream 502/503 and connection reset on health-checked serving runtime endpoints. SRE and Support saw correlated spikes in KV cache eviction and CPU utilization on a small subset of serving instances. Expected behavior: stable <0.1% 5xx for pinned model version across bursts.

Customer impact: partial failures for CartoStream users; some batch inference jobs retried and incurred extra cost. Customer reported degradation to their CS contact at 2026-03-09 13:25 UTC.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use customer API key for CartoStream (dedicated pool).
2) Send 250 concurrent short-chat generation requests (max_tokens=128) with high prefix overlap (same 3 prompts repeated) over 3 minutes to /v1/generate.
3) Observe increased 5xx responses and occasional connection resets.

Notes: traffic profile simulates a small burst with high KV cache contention due to identical prefixes across concurrent sessions.
logs: Sample request ids with 5xx: req_0a7b2e (13:13:04 UTC) -> 502 upstream-reset; req_0a7b98 (13:13:07 UTC) -> 503 kube-probe-fail; req_0a7c10 (13:23:01 UTC) -> 502 kernel-conn-reset. API gateway traces show 504 -> timeout to backend preceeded by 'stream closed: remote peer reset' and repeated 'cache-miss flood' entries in serving-runtime logs. See S3 logs: s3://redwood-logs/prod/us-east/2026-03-09/cartostream/ and grafana dashboard panel: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/serving/errors?orgId=1&from=2026-03-09T13:00:00Z&to=2026-03-09T14:00:00Z
comments: 2026-03-09 13:30 UTC - Lucas Moreno: Triage started. Noticed KV eviction spikes on 3 nodes hosting CartoStream slices. Hypothesis: small dedicated pool + identical prefixes -> KV-cache thrash causing elevated CPU and occasional runtime OOM/restarts.

2026-03-09 13:42 UTC - SRE Oncall (Maya Chen): Correlated runtime container restarts on node gke-prod-e-7b12 with oom_kill in system logs. API gateway shows upstream 502s for these endpoints. Increasing pod replica count for the serving pool improved error rate in staging test but production still impacted for a short window.

2026-03-09 14:05 UTC - Support (Sana Patel): Informed customer of ongoing investigation and recommended temporary mitigation: reduce concurrency to 80 and add jitter to request prefixes while we stabilize. Customer accepted and applied client-side throttling.

2026-03-09 15:10 UTC - Lucas Moreno: Deployed a change to cache-manager to limit aggressive TTL churn (hot-key backoff) as an emergency mitigation; rolling restart of 4 smaller hosts in the dedicated pool scheduled. Observed 5xx rate drop from 12% -> 0.9% over 20 minutes.

2026-03-11 09:22 UTC - Maya Chen: Postmortem draft linked. Root cause appears to be combined: (1) workload with high identical-prefix concurrency, (2) small dedicated pool sizing, (3) a regression in cache eviction policy introduced in runtime PR #1011 that lowered hot-key protections.
investigation_notes:
- Reproduced locally with stress test harness that simulates identical prefix workloads; confirmed KV cache miss storm and eviction spikes leading to increased CPU and occasional runtime panics.
- JVM/native runtime stack traces show heavy LRU churn and 'null pointer deref' in cache clean-up path visible in runtime logs around 13:12 UTC.
- Runtime PR #1011 merged 2026-03-06 changed eviction aggressiveness for low-mem instances; appears to be the regression vector.
- Node gke-prod-e-7b12 had slightly older kernel with known connection reset under heavy socket churn; contributed to connection resets but not primary cause.
- No evidence of DDoS or malicious traffic; pattern was customer workload characteristics.
mitigation:
Immediate: increased replica count for the customer's dedicated serving pool by 50%, applied emergency hot-key backoff settings in cache-manager, and restarted the 3 affected runtime pods. Recommended customer action: apply client-side jitter and limit concurrency to recommended thresholds.
Short-term: revert PR #1011 behavior for low-memory instances and push hotfix to runtime (PR linked).
Long-term: implement automatic detection of hot-key thrash and adaptive per-customer cache throttling, add preemptive scaling triggers for high-prefix-overlap workloads.
resolution: 2026-03-11 - Hotfix deployed (runtime PR #1024) that restores previous hot-key backoff logic and adds defensive null-checks in cache cleanup. Dedicated pool resized for CartoStream and autoscaling policy adjusted. Post-deploy monitoring shows error rate returned to baseline (<0.2%) and no further restarts. Customer notified and offered a credit for excess failed requests; they accepted. Postmortem page created and follow-up epic INT-892 opened for cache-thrashing detection and autoscale improvements.
